cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). He's just reminded them that Christ died for our sins, was buried, and was raised on the third day (1 Corinthians 15:3-4). But some of them are saying something about the dead, and I bet Paul's eyebrows went up higher than mine do when somebody asks for a cookie with NO chocolate chips.

cards.question: It's preached that Christ has been raised from the dead. What are some people in Corinth saying?

answers.text: There is no resurrection of the dead
Paul is not a real apostle

cards.question: Some in Corinth say there is no resurrection of the dead. Paul says that even then, Christ could still have been raised.

cards.text: So Paul follows that idea all the way out, like pulling one loose thread on a sweater, friend. If Christ has not been raised, two things become worthless right along with it.

cards.question: If Christ has not been raised, which two things does Paul say are worthless?

cards.text: Now it gets personal for Paul. He and the others have testified about God that He raised Christ from the dead, and they put their NAMES on that, the way I put mine on every cookie box I seal.

cards.question: If the dead are not raised, what does Paul say that would make him and the others?

cards.text: Paul says it again: if the dead are not raised, not even Christ has been raised. Some things you say twice, friend, like "that oven is HOT," and this time he adds that the Corinthians' faith would be futile.

cards.question: If Christ has not been raised, Paul tells the Corinthians they are still in their sins.

cards.text: Then Paul thinks about the believers who have already died, the ones he calls those who have fallen asleep in Christ. I think that thought would hurt anybody who's ever lost someone.

cards.question: If Christ wasn't raised, Paul says those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

cards.text: Then Paul zooms WAY out and puts himself in the picture: what if our hope in Christ is for this life alone? Picture buying the best seat in the house for a show, and finding out there IS no show.

cards.question: If their hope in Christ is for this life alone, Paul says believers are to be ___ more than all men.

cards.text: Then Paul flips it. After all those ifs, he's ready to say what's REALLY true, and SOMEBODY get this man a microphone!

cards.question: After all those ifs, what does Paul now say about Christ?

answers.text: He has indeed been raised from the dead
He will be raised from the dead one day
He lives on only in our memories

cards.text: Paul calls the risen Christ "the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep." Firstfruits, friend. Hold on to that word.
Paul takes it WAY back, friend, before ovens, before bakeries, before anybody ever said the word cookie. Death came through a man.

cards.question: Since death came through a man, Paul says the resurrection of the dead comes through the angels.

cards.text: That man is Adam, the first man, and Paul sets him right next to Christ. Two names, two very different batches.

cards.question: Paul says in Adam all die, and in Christ all will be made ___.

cards.text: But Paul says there's an order to it, each in his own turn. Like my oven, friend: the first batch comes out, THEN the next one.

cards.question: Christ goes first as the firstfruits. Then at His coming, who does Paul say comes next?

cards.text: Then, Paul says, the end will come, when Christ hands over the kingdom to God the Father after destroying all dominion, authority and power. That's why my ovens stay ready, friend.

cards.question: Paul says Christ must reign until something happens. Until what?

answers.text: Until all His enemies are under His feet
Until the day of Pentecost comes
Until the last apostle has died

cards.question: Paul says the last enemy to be destroyed is ___.

cards.text: Paul quotes Psalm 8:6: "God has put everything under His feet." He adds that this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him, and friend, this man doesn't leave a single crumb of room for confusion.

cards.question: Paul says that when all things have been subjected to Him, the Son Himself will be made subject to the One who put all things under Him, so that God may be all in all.

cards.text: Paul comes at it from ANOTHER angle, and this man has more angles than Berry, one of my cookie cutter kids, and Berry is a STAR. He points to people who are baptized for the dead.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians to stop being baptized for the dead.

cards.text: Then Paul turns it on himself and the others: why would they put themselves in danger every hour? Every HOUR, friend, and my mustache starts shaking when the oven timer hits one minute.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians he faces death every ___.

cards.text: Paul says he faces death every day, as surely as he boasts about the Corinthians in Christ Jesus our Lord. Then he asks, "If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for human motives, what did I gain?"

cards.question: If the dead are not raised, what way of living does Paul say might as well take over?

answers.text: Live it up since tomorrow we die
Work hard since the end is near
Stay quiet since no one is listening

cards.question: Paul warns the Corinthians not to be deceived, and says bad company corrupts good character.

cards.text: Then Paul rings a wake-up call LOUDER than Ruby ever rang, and Ruby, one of my cookie cutter kids, was the loudest bell in the whole kitchen: "Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning…"

cards.question: Why does Paul tell the Corinthians to sober up and stop sinning?

answers.text: Some of them are ignorant of God
Some of them are leaving the church
Some of them are too proud to pray

cards.text: Paul tells them, "I say this to your shame." But don't close the cookie box yet, friend, because he's not finished teaching on this.
